title: Impinj M700-Series UHF Inlays — RAIN RFID, -22.7 dBm
summary: Impinj M700-series UHF inlays deliver read sensitivity down to −22.7 dBm for RAIN RFID (EPC Gen2v2) tagging in dry, wet and converted-label formats. The family spans {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} (retail EPC), {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} (−22.1 dBm, logistics with user memory) and {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} (high memory plus AutoTune for mixed surfaces). It is the volume chip family behind the Walmart RFID mandate, retail item-level programmes, warehouse pallet portals and healthcare instrument tracking, with a pin-compatible M800 upgrade path.

brief.label: M700 family — {chip:impinj-m730:short_name}, {chip:impinj-m750:short_name}, {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} positioning
items: {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} — mainstream retail workhorse: 96-bit EPC, minimal user memory, the volume chip for retail item-level programmes where the EPC serial is what matters. Default for apparel, footwear, beauty, and general-merchandise tagging.

{chip:impinj-m750:short_name} — volume production with user memory: 128-bit EPC + user memory suitable for on-tag lot codes, date codes, or limited serialization payloads. The tier most logistics and healthcare programmes ship against.

{chip:impinj-m770:short_name} — high memory + AutoTune: largest user memory in the M700 family + AutoTune for consistent performance across mixed mounting surfaces (metal, liquid, cardboard) without specifying an on-metal-specific antenna.

All three within ~0.6 dB of each other — {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} at −22.7 dBm, {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} at −22.1 dBm per Impinj M700 series datasheet; antenna design and mounting surface dominate in-use range variation.

brief.label: Air interface and standards
items: ISO/IEC 18000-63 / EPC Gen2v2 air interface; full Gen2v2 base command set including Untraceable on {chip:impinj-m770:short_name}.
GS1 EPC Tag Data Standard (TDS) encoding for SGTIN, SSCC, GIAI, GLN identifiers.
RAIN RFID Alliance certified across reader and infrastructure ecosystem.

Free-air bench 10-15 m with 6 dBic antenna at 4 W EIRP; real-world 5-10 m handheld retail, 3-8 m fixed-portal warehouse, 2-4 m healthcare small-item.

{chip:impinj-m730:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} family — pure-EPC retail ({chip:impinj-m730:short_name}), mainstream logistics + user memory ({chip:impinj-m750:short_name}), high-memory + AutoTune mixed-surface ({chip:impinj-m770:short_name}). All share the same sensitivity floor; antenna design and mounting surface dominate in-use range variation. ARC Master List + Walmart RFID + Auburn RFID Lab benchmark certified.

Dry / wet / converted-label form factors across 15+ standard antenna designs (general-purpose, compact pharma / jewellery, on-metal, on-liquid, windshield, tire, woven care label, hang-tag) + custom antenna engineering 4-8 weeks. Pin- and protocol-compatible upgrade path to M800-series ({chip:impinj-m830:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m850:short_name}) for Gen2X features, ~1-2 dB sensitivity gain, and ~30% lower chip power without antenna re-tune or reader-fleet re-qualification.

sections.title: What an M700 inlay actually is
sections.intro: Strip away the face stock, the print and the die-cut and what actually answers the reader is deceptively small: an Impinj M700-series chip flip-mounted onto a metal strap, bonded to an etched-aluminium dipole antenna on a PET web. That is the inlay — a sub-component, not a finished label — resonating across the global UHF RAIN band of 860-960 MHz that each region then carves into its own narrower window. On the generic inlay hub the silicon is treated as interchangeable; on this SKU it is the whole specification. The M700's −22.7 dBm read sensitivity is why the same antenna reads 15-30% further than it did on the M600-series predecessor — and the antenna geometry is the part you actually tune around it.
bullets: 15+ standard antenna designs: general-purpose far-field, compact (jewellery / pharma), on-metal, on-liquid, windshield, tire, woven care label, hang-tag.
Custom antenna engineering 4-8 weeks for specialised applications — provide target read range, tag dimensions, mounting surface, environmental conditions.
Smartrac, Avery Dennison, ARC Master List-certified antenna designs available across the M700 portfolio.

image.alt: Annotated anatomy of an Impinj M700-series UHF RFID inlay: the M700 chip on a metal strap at the centre of an etched-aluminium dipole antenna, carried on a PET web, reading at −22.7 dBm sensitivity and tuned across the 860-960 MHz UHF band.

sections.title: Wet, dry, converted: one M700 inlay, three finish states
sections.intro: The same M700 chip and antenna leave the line in one of three finish states, and which one you order is dictated entirely by the process waiting downstream. A dry inlay is the bare core; a wet inlay adds the pressure-sensitive adhesive and release liner a label converter laminates from; a converted label is that inlay already built into printed face stock — at which point it has stopped being a component and become a finished branded label.
bullets: Dry inlay: bare antenna + chip on a carrier substrate, no adhesive. For label converters laminating into their own label construction.
Wet inlay: pressure-sensitive adhesive on release liner, ready to apply to any surface.
Converted label: printed face stock (paper, PET, polypropylene) + adhesive + inlay; finished branded label ready for end-use application.

image.alt: Three finish states of one Impinj M700 inlay, left to right: a dry inlay with no adhesive or liner for converter lamination, a wet inlay adding a pressure-sensitive adhesive layer and a release liner, and a converted label with the inlay built into printed face stock as a finished branded label.

sections.title: Why M700 chip selection drives UHF deployment performance

items.label: Free-air bench range (6 dBic / 4 W EIRP)

bullets: Read range in real-world environments runs 30-50% shorter than lab specifications. Building materials, metal shelving, liquid products, and dense item stacking attenuate UHF; chip sensitivity compensates.

Dense reader environments (retail stores with multiple zones, warehouses with multiple portals) create RF interference. High-sensitivity chip maintains reliable reads in noisy RF where older chips experience read failures.

Small-antenna inlays for compact labels (jewellery, pharmaceutical, small-item) deliver proportionally shorter read range; the M700's enhanced sensitivity recovers 20-40% of the range lost to antenna miniaturisation.

Item-level tagging programmes in retail and healthcare require 99.5%+ read rates at operational speeds. Marginal improvements in chip sensitivity translate directly to fewer missed reads and higher deployment ROI.

sections.title: Datasheet range vs in-use range — derating rule of thumb

dataHighlight.heading: Real-world range derating from free-air datasheet by application
dataHighlight.text: Free-air datasheet range (10-15 m with 6 dBic CP antenna at 4 W EIRP) routinely overstates in-use performance by 2-4×. Retail apparel floor: divide by 2× for handheld 5-8 m and fixed-zone 3-5 m coverage. Warehouse dock-door portal: divide by 3× for 3-6 m portal coverage with 99.5%+ read rate at forklift speeds. Healthcare and pharma: divide by 4× — small antenna footprints required for vials / blister packs / blood bags + aqueous drug attenuation reduce range to 2-4 m. The physics is consistent: building materials + metal shelving + liquid products + multi-tag collision all attenuate UHF differently from open-air bench testing. Always validate with on-site pilot before committing to antenna choice. Auburn University RFID Lab certifications under the Walmart-aligned ARC Master List specifications are the standard procurement reference for retail-grade performance benchmarks.
dataHighlight.source: Auburn University RFID Lab ARC Master List + Proud Tek deployment references

bullets: Bench: 10-15 m free-air with 6 dBic CP antenna at 4 W EIRP.
Retail apparel: 5-10 m handheld at walking speed, 2-5 m fixed-zone.
Warehouse dock door: 3-6 m per portal, 99.5%+ read at 1-2 m/s forklift speed.
Healthcare / pharma: 2-4 m typical due to small antenna + aqueous attenuation.
Rule of thumb: divide datasheet range by 2× retail, 3× warehouse, 4× healthcare.

sections.title: From EPC Gen2 v1 2004 to M700-series as RAIN RFID volume floor

items.text: EPC Gen2 v1 standardised through EPCglobal; ISO/IEC 18000-63 Type C ratified subsequently. The protocol that every UHF inlay shipped today implements at the air-interface layer.

Walmart Phase 1 RFID pilot establishes the apparel item-level operational template; Inditex (Zara) deploys at brand-portfolio scale; supply-chain DC-portal programmes scale on {chip:impinj-monza-r6:short_name}-class chips.

ISO/IEC 18000-63 Amendment 1 publishes, adding the optional AUTHENTICATE command framework to EPC Gen2v2. The standard framework exists; mainstream RAIN RFID silicon (Impinj M700 / M800, {chip:nxp-ucode-8:name} / 9, {chip:alien-higgs-9:name}) does not currently implement it as a shipping crypto feature — programmes needing per-tap cryptographic authentication today specify HF chips such as {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:name}.

Impinj M700-series ships with −22.7 dBm read sensitivity ({chip:impinj-m730:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name}; {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} -22.1 dBm) — 15-30% longer range vs M600 predecessor; ARC Master List benchmarks at Auburn University RFID Lab establish the procurement-reference performance envelope.

Walmart RFID source-tag mandate scales to apparel across all suppliers; {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} emerges as the volume retail-floor chip; Macy's, Nike, Inditex, Lululemon mandates align on the same encoding / chip stack.

Walmart mandate expands to home / electronics / beauty / hardline; {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} ship into 5+ new retail-floor categories simultaneously. ATA Spec 2000 + DSCSA pharmaceutical adjacencies adopt {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} for user-memory-on-tag programmes.

items.label: 2026 Today
items.text: Operating-playbook notes for retail-apparel-item-level, supply-chain-pallet, healthcare-asset-tracking, manufacturing-WIP, and aerospace-MRO programmes converge on {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} (pure-EPC retail) / {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} (logistics + user memory) / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} (mixed-surface) at the chip layer + ARC-certified antenna at the inlay layer + dry / wet / converted-label form factor matched to converter or end-user workflow as the operator-side template. M800 ({chip:impinj-m830:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m850:short_name}) upgrade path runs in parallel for next-gen power efficiency and Gen2X protocol features on the same antenna designs.

sections.title: The reference facts, at a glance
sections.intro: Everything a converter or programme reviewer cross-checks against the datasheet — sensitivity and range, the real-world derating rule, memory architecture, retail and Walmart mandate fit, the healthcare and aerospace programme notes, the M700 → M800 upgrade path and procurement — gathered into one scannable block.

features.title: Read sensitivity & range
features.text: −22.7 dBm (M730 / M770) / −22.1 dBm (M750) read sensitivity at the chip — 15-30% longer read range than M600-series predecessor in identical antenna designs. Free-air bench: 10-15 m read range with 6 dBic CP antenna at 4 W EIRP. Real-world envelopes: 5-10 m handheld in retail, 3-8 m fixed-portal in warehouse, 2-4 m on healthcare small-item / liquid-adjacent / on-metal applications.

features.title: Real-world range derating
features.text: Retail apparel floor: divide datasheet range by 2× for actual operational read. Warehouse cases / pallet: divide by 3× — pallet contents, stretch-wrap, tag orientation all attenuate. Healthcare / pharma: divide by 4× — small antenna footprints, aqueous drug attenuation, dense packaging. On-metal / on-liquid: factor in 50-70% range reduction vs free-air; specify on-metal-tuned antenna or M770 AutoTune for consistency.

features.title: Memory architecture
features.text: M730: 128-bit EPC (configurable to 96-bit for SGTIN) + 96-bit serialised TID; no user memory. M750: 96-bit EPC + 96-bit serialised TID + 32-bit user memory (for short lot / date codes). M770: 128-bit EPC + 96-bit serialised TID + 64-bit user memory + Protected Mode + AutoTune. 32-bit access password + 32-bit kill password on all variants per EPC Gen2v2.

features.title: Walmart & retail mandate fit
features.text: Walmart RFID source-tagging mandate (apparel since 2020, expanded to home / electronics / beauty 2022-2024) requires SGTIN encoding per GS1 TDS — M730 is the volume chip for source-tag compliance. ARC Master List spec category compliance (apparel, footwear, hard goods) — Auburn University RFID Lab benchmarks are the procurement reference. Adjacent retail mandates: Target, Macy's, Inditex, Nike, Lululemon, Kohl's all run on the same chip / antenna / encoding stack.

features.title: Healthcare & pharmaceutical use
features.text: DSCSA (U.S. Drug Supply Chain Security Act) + EU FMD (Falsified Medicines Directive) — RFID-on-pack pharmaceutical traceability with M730 / M750. Surgical instrument tracking, blood-bag identification, specimen-slide labelling — small-antenna inlays with high-sensitivity M700 chip recover range lost to miniaturisation. Healthcare RTLS adjacency — UHF inlays + ceiling readers for instrument / asset / patient-flow tracking.

features.title: Aerospace & supply-chain MRO
features.text: ATA Spec 2000 Chapter 9-5 RFID for aviation parts traceability; Boeing / Airbus tier-1 supplier requirement on rotable parts. Spec 2000 EPC encoding + serialised TID for unique-part identification across the part lifecycle. M750 with user memory for on-tag part-history payload where backend connectivity is unreliable.

features.title: M700 → M800 upgrade path
features.text: Pin- and protocol-compatible: inlays qualified on M700 antenna designs swap to M830 (128-bit EPC, no user memory) or M850 (96-bit EPC + 32-bit user memory) without antenna re-tune or reader-fleet re-qualification. M800 adds Gen2X protocol features (faster inventory, improved data integrity, optional Protected Mode for privacy / supply-chain serialisation control). ~1-2 dB sensitivity improvement (10-20% longer read range) and 30% lower power consumption at the chip level enable smaller / on-metal / on-liquid inlays that struggled on M700. Plan M700 → M800 transition 4-8 weeks ahead for stock antenna designs (production line continues unchanged) — longer if new antenna tooling is required.

features.title: Procurement & validation
features.text: Prototype quantities: 100-1,000 units; production: 100M+ units / year. On-site pilot validation recommended before committing to antenna choice — bench specs over-state real-world range; divide datasheet by 2-4× depending on application. Lead time: 4-6 weeks for standard antenna designs; 8-12 weeks for custom antenna development + production qualification.

faq.question: What is the read range of the Impinj M700 inlay?
faq.answer: Read range depends on antenna design and application environment. Free-air bench: 10-15 m with a standard 6 dBic CP antenna at 4 W EIRP. Real-world: 5-10 m handheld in retail, 3-8 m fixed-portal in warehouse, 2-4 m on healthcare small-item / on-liquid / on-metal applications. Always derate datasheet range by 2× for retail, 3× warehouse, 4× healthcare. Validate with on-site pilot before committing to antenna choice.

faq.question: What is the difference between dry inlay, wet inlay, and converted label?
faq.answer: Dry inlay: bare antenna + chip on a carrier substrate, no adhesive — for label converters laminating into their own construction. Wet inlay: pressure-sensitive adhesive on release liner, ready to apply directly. Converted label: printed face stock (paper, PET, polypropylene) + adhesive + inlay = finished branded label ready for end-use. Choose dry for converter integration, wet for direct application, converted for branded-label end-use.

faq.question: Can I get the M700 in a custom antenna design?
faq.answer: Yes — beyond 15+ standard antenna designs, custom antenna engineering for specialised applications. Provide target read range, tag dimensions, mounting surface material, and environmental conditions; RF engineering team designs and prototypes a custom antenna optimised for the use case. Typical custom antenna development: 4-8 weeks. ARC Master List + Auburn University RFID Lab certification available for retail-grade performance benchmarks.

faq.question: Which M700 variant should I specify for a new apparel item-level programme?
faq.answer: Pure-EPC apparel rollout (no on-tag user data, EPC is the handle into cloud item master): {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} — volume choice, lowest per-unit cost. {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} if encoding workflow writes lot / date codes / short serial into user memory alongside EPC. {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} if same SKU family applies across mixed surfaces (some apparel, some on-metal hang-tags, some on liquid-containing gift sets) where AutoTune earns its premium. {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} share −22.7 dBm sensitivity; {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} sits at −22.1 dBm — swapping {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} ↔ {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} mid-programme costs ~0.6 dB at the chip level, mostly absorbed by antenna design margin.

faq.question: What is the migration path from M700 to M800?
faq.answer: Pin- and protocol-compatible. Inlays qualified on M700 antenna designs rebuild with M830 ({chip:impinj-m830:epc_bits}-bit EPC, no user memory) or M850 ({chip:impinj-m850:epc_bits}-bit EPC + {chip:impinj-m850:user_bits}-bit user memory) chips on the identical antenna without antenna re-tune, reader-fleet re-qualification, or production-line encoding / print-apply re-validation. M800 family adds Gen2X protocol features (faster inventory, improved data integrity), ~30% lower chip power consumption, ~1-2 dB sensitivity improvement, and optional Impinj Protected Mode for privacy / supply-chain serialisation control. Plan M700 → M800 transition 4-8 weeks ahead for stock antenna designs; longer if new antenna tooling is required.

faq.question: How does the M700 compare to NXP UCODE and Alien Higgs?
faq.answer: M700 ({chip:impinj-m750:read_sensitivity_dbm} to {chip:impinj-m730:read_sensitivity_dbm} dBm sensitivity across M730 / M750 / M770 variants) is the volume retail / logistics chip; ARC Master List dominant. NXP UCODE 8 / 9 ({chip:nxp-ucode-8:read_sensitivity_dbm} / {chip:nxp-ucode-9:read_sensitivity_dbm} dBm respectively) is the European-incumbent alternative, also Walmart-mandate compatible; UCODE 9 has the best-in-class sensitivity of the volume RAIN tier and is the choice for freezer / dense-reader / long-range applications. {chip:alien-higgs-9:name} offers {chip:alien-higgs-9:user_bits}-bit user memory (largest in commodity UHF) at slightly higher sensitivity than M700 ({chip:alien-higgs-9:read_sensitivity_dbm} dBm typical); the right answer when on-tag user data dominates the use case. Detailed compare on the UCODE-vs-UCODE-vs-Monza-vs-Higgs page.
